_about: The tutorial script. Each step: what the characters say, then (optionally) a task the player must do before the next step. Speakers are character codes from the Characters page; {player}, {teacher} and {hacker} become names. Goals: placed:<item>, owns:<item>, link:<item>:<item>.

say: {player}! Thank goodness I found you. It’s me, {teacher}, from your dad’s datacentre.
Three nights ago DataTech raided us. {lucas} used his Reapers to do his dirty work, and they took your dad. NetForge is gone.
Lawyers won’t beat DataTech. Networks will. Learn everything your dad knew, build your own datacentre, and grow big enough to buy DataTech out from under {lucas}.
Then we walk in the front door and bring {dad} home.
It starts here, in your garage, with one laptop. Let’s get it online, so it starts earning credits for you.
First, the laptop. Open your inventory (I), click the laptop, then click the glowing spot on the workbench. You’ll carry it over yourself.
steps.task: Place your laptop on the workbench.

say: Nice! A laptop on its own can’t reach the internet, though. It needs a router.
Open the shop (B) and buy a home router. You started with enough credits for one.
steps.task: Buy a home router in the shop.

say: Got it. Put it on the shelf: pick it in your inventory, then click the glowing shelf spot.
steps.task: Place the home router on the shelf.

say: Devices talk through cables. Buy a pack of copper cable: that’s the straight-through kind, for joining a router to the ISP box and your laptop.
steps.task: Buy a pack of copper cable.

say: Now the important bit. That box on the wall is the ISP box: your connection to the internet.
Pick the cable tool (C). Click the ISP box and choose its LAN port, then click your router and choose its WAN port.
steps.task: Cable the ISP box’s LAN port to the router’s WAN port.

say: The router’s online! Last link: plug your laptop’s Eth0 port into one of the router’s LAN ports.
steps.task: Cable the laptop to a router LAN port.

say: You’re online! See the coins popping out? Your network now earns credits every second. Watch the wallet at the top.
The laptop does the earning. Routers and switches earn nothing themselves, but every device behind them earns more: your router adds 25%.
Spend them in the shop, but it only sells what your level allows. You level up by learning: press L for lessons.
Be a shame if someone… came knocking.
Ignore them. That’s {hacker}, and they’ll be back. Learn your lessons and you’ll stop every attack.
That’s the basics. Open Learn (L) whenever you’re ready. Good luck!

attack: Found a door. Mind if I come in?
_moments: Tips the characters give along the way, each shown once. {item}, {price}, {level}, {place}, {list}, {why} are filled in by the game.

cable:copper: Copper straight-through cable, the everyday one. The wires run pin 1 to pin 1, end to end.
Use it between unlike devices: a laptop or PC to a router’s LAN port or a switch, or your router’s WAN port to the ISP box.
cable:crossover: A crossover cable swaps the send and receive wires inside the cable.
That’s for like devices: switch to switch, router to router, PC to PC. Plug unlike devices with it and the link stays down.
cable:fiber: Fiber carries light, not electricity. It’s fast, goes much further than copper and ignores electrical noise.
It only fits fiber ports: the Gi ports on rack gear and the datacentre’s ISP panel. Either end can plug into either side.
cable:console: The console cable isn’t a network link. It plugs into a device’s console port so you can type commands into it directly.
That’s how you set up a new router or switch before it’s on the network. No traffic flows over it, so it earns nothing.
port:mdi: See the host-style ports? That’s MDI: laptops, PCs, servers and a router’s WAN port. They send on one pair of wires and listen on the other.
Host-style to switch-style takes a straight-through cable. Host to host needs a crossover.
port:mdix: Switch-style ports (MDI-X) are on switches and a home router’s LAN side. They swap send and receive for you.
So: host to switch, straight-through. Switch to switch, crossover.
port:wan: This one has a WAN port and LAN ports. WAN faces the outside world: run it to the ISP box. LAN ports face your own devices.
port:fiber: That Gi port is fiber: a Gigabit port that takes light. Only a fiber cable fits it.
port:console: That’s a console port, for managing the device with a console cable. It never carries network traffic.
afford: Hey {player}, you’ve saved up enough for a {item} now: {price} credits. {why}
It’s in the shop (B). I’ve opened it for you.
unlock: Level {level}! That unlocks new gear in the shop: {list}.
lease: {player}, you can afford to lease the {place} now. More room means more gear, and more income.
Click where you are, top left, to lease it. Your garage stays yours: you can travel back any time.
arrive:office: Welcome to the office! Desks for PCs out front, and a server room behind the glass with six rack slots.
Run the new ISP box to a router or switch, then plug your gear into that.
One more thing. Word gets around when a business grows. Investors will text you offers, and a broker called {broker} likes to hang around new offices.
His deals are often good. Often. Keep an eye on your wallet.
arrive:datacentre: The datacentre! Two long rack rows and fiber straight from the provider.
The ISP panel here is fiber only, so you’ll need fiber cables and gear with Gi ports.
gpu: GPUs are in the shop now. Rigs go in a rack and earn on their own; cards go inside a server and boost what it earns.
Three sellers: ByteBay is cheap but slower, Apex is the fastest and priciest. Their prices move and stock refills every 20 minutes, so shop around.
furniture: Running out of spots? Buy furniture in the shop. A desk adds a spot for a PC, a server rack adds a slot for rack gear.
Click it in your inventory, then an open bit of floor. Use the remove tool to pick it up again.
wifi: That one connects over Wi-Fi, so there's no cable to run. It needs an access point online in the same room: a wireless router, an AP-PT, or a lightweight AP with its controller.
Small devices like phones, sensors and access points can stand on any open bit of floor. Click it in your inventory, then a free tile.
lap: A lightweight access point is clever but helpless on its own. It needs a Wireless LAN Controller online in the same building to give it its settings.
Put a WLC in a rack, cable both to your switch, and every LAP in the building comes alive.
broker: Psst. {player}, right? Nice little operation you’ve got.
I know people at the GPU suppliers. A little cash up front and I can get you a discount on every GPU. Want my help?
broker:deal: Pleasure doing business. {pct}% off every GPU for the next {minutes} minutes. Go shopping.
broker:scam: Sure, sure. Hold on, I just need to check your… wallet.
{player}! He just lifted {amount} credits and vanished. Grey-market deals are a gamble.
broker:refused: Suit yourself. You know where to find me.
